meta.temperature_K_convention: Pair is [min_K, max_K]. Use null for max to mean no upper bound. A number always means that number — there is no magic threshold. (999 is still read as no-bound for older files, but is deprecated: write null.)

general.description: Extremophile organisms that form hardened shield-like structures to protect against stellar radiation. These shields are synthesized from surrounding inorganic material and help condense and channel trace atmospheric liquids, enabling survival in extremely arid environments.

meta.summary: Extremophile organisms that form hardened shield-like structures to protect against stellar radiation. These shields are synthesized from surrounding inorganic material and help condense and channel trace atmospheric liquids, enabling survival in extremely arid environments.

color_variants.rule: Color depends on parent star type (applies to all species)

species.description: Species with a broad tear-shaped shield that protects against extreme sunlight and channels water droplets into the soil.
Produces a curved, pearl-like shield housing up to three central organisms on a bed of leaves.
Angular shield with a reflective outer surface protecting spiky organisms; adapted for distant orbital positions.

distance_from_star.soft_below_note: Corpus 2026-10-03: of 5,974 speculumi bodies, 43 at 2,400-2,500 ls, 21 at 2,300-2,400, 12 at 2,000-2,300, none nearer; per ls that is 0.14, 0.07 and 0.015 of the density just past 2,500. Kept at that chance instead of demoted.

core_requirements: Rocky or High Metal Content planets only

species_specific_rules.extra_requirement: Must be located at least 2500 LS (~5 AU) from parent star

authorNotes.temperature_constraints: All species require temperature above 190K (global rule)
special_rules: No atmosphere-based species split (all species share same atmospheres)
Distance from star is the ONLY species-specific differentiator (speculumi)
Color is fully determined by parent star type
One of the simplest genera structurally (uniform conditions across species)
Planet type restriction is implicit via atmosphere (Rocky / High Metal Content only)
